subject: Business Models
title: API Platforms
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: API Platforms.

hook.text: Stripe lets any developer accept payments with a few lines of code. It's a platform for money.

buildup.text: API platforms provide infrastructure as a service. Developers build on top; the platform handles complexity.

discovery.text: Twilio (communications), Stripe (payments), and Plaid (banking data) are invisible layers powering millions of apps.

twist.text: Once embedded, API platforms are almost impossible to rip out. Switching costs are enormous.

climax.text: API platforms profit from the success of every app built on them. They're the picks and shovels.

punchline.text: Build the layer everyone needs. Let others build on top of you.

quiz.question: Why are API platforms hard to displace once adopted?

details.summary: API platforms expose programmable interfaces that let external developers build applications and integrations on top of platform infrastructure. Stripe for payments, Twilio for communications, and AWS for cloud computing all generate enormous ecosystems through their APIs.
details.whyItMatters: API platforms create powerful developer ecosystems that extend functionality far beyond what the platform company could build alone. Each integration deepens switching costs and network effects as the ecosystem becomes indispensable infrastructure.
takeaways: APIs let external developers build on platform infrastructure
Developer ecosystems create powerful compounding network effects
API platforms become deeply embedded infrastructure with high switching costs

faq.question: Why are API platforms so difficult to displace once established?
faq.answer: Developers integrate APIs deeply into their applications' core logic. Switching requires rewriting code, retesting, and risking downtime. The more applications built on an API, the more the platform benefits from ecosystem lock-in that makes displacement extremely costly.

faq.question: How do API platforms monetize their developer ecosystems?
faq.answer: Usage-based pricing charges per API call, transaction, or data volume. Tiered plans offer increasing capabilities at higher prices. Some offer free tiers that convert to paid as developers scale. Revenue share models take a percentage of transactions processed through the API.
